1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

1	---
2	name: horizon-start
3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
4	---
5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.
71	
72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TwoChartRepresentable
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TwoChartHonest
8	
9	/-!
10	# A CHART-TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS IS TRIVIAL WHEN THE OVERLAP UNITS ARE ALL COBOUNDARIES
11	
12	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of
13	the two-chart comparison
14	
15	```
16	Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  ↪  X.CechPic
17	```
18	
19	— surjectivity onto the chart-trivial classes (`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial`,
20	`Tangent/TwoChartRepresentable.lean:301`) and the exact kernel
21	(`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`, `Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean:321`).  Composing them
22	gives a **criterion** nobody had stated: if every overlap unit is a coboundary, then every class
23	trivial on both charts is trivial.
24	
25	That composite is what a computation of `Pic` on a two-chart cover actually wants to consume: it
26	turns a statement about the *unit groups of three rings* — pure commutative algebra, no
27	cohomology — into triviality of a Picard class.  Both inputs are general in the scheme, so this
28	is too: no affineness, no curve, no dual numbers, no field.
29	
30	## Why it is here rather than in `Tangent/`
31	
32	The two inputs were built for the Wave-5 `ε`-kernel computation and live there.  This file is
33	about the *Picard group of a two-chart scheme* rather than about tangent spaces, and its intended
34	consumer is the ring-case obligation of the representability route
35	(`Picard/Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean`), where the relevant `X` is a relative curve over a test ring
36	and the three rings are the two chart algebras and their overlap.
37	
38	## The one hypothesis that is not about units
39	
40	`hsel`, surjectivity of the selector, is what makes the two-chart cover *honest* (both charts are
41	actually used).  It is not an extra obligation:
42	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine`
43	(`Tangent/TwoChartHonest.lean:108`) derives it from `¬ IsAffine X` alone, and a proper
44	positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not affine.  Stated with `hsel` explicit because this
45	file is general in `X` and the non-affineness is the consumer's to supply.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48	
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the
50	  criterion.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the same as a
52	  statement about the subgroup of chart-trivial classes, for a consumer holding two classes
53	  rather than one.
54	-/
55	
56	set_option autoImplicit false
57	
58	universe u
59	
60	open CategoryTheory
61	
62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	namespace Scheme
65	
66	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : Bool → X.Opens}
67	
68	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the overlap units of a two-chart cover: the units of
69	`Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` that are products of restrictions of chart units.  Abbreviation for the
70	`TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two restriction maps, so that the statements below read. -/
71	noncomputable abbrev twoChartCoboundaryUnits (V : Bool → X.Opens) :
72	    Subgroup Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ :=
73	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
74	    (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
75	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
76	
77	/-- **THE CRITERION**: on a two-chart cover whose overlap units are *all* coboundaries, a Picard
78	class trivial on both charts is trivial.
79	
80	Composite of the two landed halves of the two-chart comparison: surjectivity presents the class
81	as `twoChartClassHom` of an overlap unit, and the kernel description kills it because that unit
82	is a coboundary by hypothesis.
83	
84	Completely general in `X`: no affineness, no curve, no field, no dual numbers.  The content is
85	that `hcob` is a statement about the unit groups of three rings — so a consumer computes
86	`Pic` on a two-chart cover by computing units, with no cohomology in sight. -/
87	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary
88	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
89	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
90	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1) :
91	    L = 1 := by
92	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial sel hmem L hL
93	  rw [← hu]
94	  exact (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr (hcob u)
95	
96	/-- The criterion for a consumer holding two classes: chart-trivial classes form a subsingleton.
97	
98	Note this is *not* `Subsingleton X.CechPic` — the chart-triviality hypothesis is on the classes,
99	not on the scheme, and a class nontrivial on a chart is untouched. -/
100	theorem subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary
101	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
102	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
103	    {L M : X.CechPic}
104	    (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
105	    (hM : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι M = 1) :
106	    L = M := by
107	  rw [cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary sel hmem hsel hcob L hL,
108	    cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary sel hmem hsel hcob M hM]
109	
110	/-- The criterion with `hsel` discharged from non-affineness, which is how a curve consumer meets
111	it: a proper positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not affine, and
112	`surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine` turns that single fact into the selector surjectivity.
113	
114	Takes the cover as an `AffineTwoCover` because that is the carrier the discharge lemma is stated
115	against. -/
116	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary_of_not_isAffine
117	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : Y.AffineTwoCover) (hY : ¬ IsAffine Y)
118	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(Y, D.boolFamily false ⊓ D.boolFamily true)ˣ,
119	      u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits D.boolFamily)
120	    (L : Y.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (D.boolFamily s).ι L = 1) :
121	    L = 1 :=
122	  cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary D.selector D.selector_mem
123	    (D.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine hY) hcob L hL
124	
125	/-! ## The form with a payable hypothesis
126	
127	The universal hypothesis `hcob` above is **false** at the case the representability route cares
128	about: for `ℙ¹` over a domain, `t` is an overlap unit and is not a coboundary
129	(`not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`, `Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`) — which is just
130	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`.  So a consumer given only the criterion above would set out to prove something
131	untrue.
132	
133	The repair is to constrain only the units that *present the class in question*, which is what
134	surjectivity hands over anyway.  Two things are worth saying about it explicitly, because the
135	obvious repair is a trap:
136	
137	* the `↔` version — "`L = 1` iff some presenting unit is a coboundary" — is **vacuous**: its
138	  forward direction takes the presenting unit to be `1`, and the chart-triviality hypothesis is
139	  never consulted (measured: the unused-variable linter flags it).  So the useful form is the
140	  implication with a `∀` over presenting units, below, where both hypotheses are consumed;
141	* that form is *strictly weaker* than `hcob`, and demonstrably so: `hcob` implies it by ignoring
142	  the presentation equation (`forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary`). -/
143	
144	/-- **THE CRITERION WITH A PAYABLE HYPOTHESIS**: a chart-trivial class is trivial as soon as
145	*every unit presenting it* is a coboundary.
146	
147	Both hypotheses are consumed — `hL` produces the presenting unit through surjectivity, and
148	`hpres` is applied to exactly that unit.  Unlike the universal form this is not refuted by
149	`ℙ¹`: there the presenting units of a *degree-zero* class are the exponent-zero Laurent units,
150	which are precisely the coboundaries (`mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff`). -/
151	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary
152	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
153	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
154	    (hpres : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
155	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V) :
156	    L = 1 := by
157	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial sel hmem L hL
158	  rw [← hu]
159	  exact (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr (hpres u hu)
160	
161	/-- The universal hypothesis implies the presenting-unit one, by ignoring the presentation
162	equation.  Recorded so that "strictly weaker" is a proved relation rather than a reading of the
163	two statements — the weakening is what makes the hypothesis payable at `ℙ¹`. -/
164	theorem forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary
165	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x))
166	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
167	    (L : X.CechPic) :
168	    ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
169	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V :=
170	  fun u _ => hcob u
171	
172	end Scheme
173	
174	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# THE RING CASE OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS ZARISKI-LOCAL ON THE TEST RING

The surviving obligation of the whole vanishing route to a `JacobianData` is a statement at
an **arbitrary** `k`-algebra `A`, in either of two interderivable spellings:

* `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` — consumed by
  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`);
* ring-level field-point rigidity `hrigAff` — consumed by `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
  (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).

This file attacks the **quantifier** rather than the content: both spellings are Zariski-local
on `Spec A`.  The input is the *separation* half of the landed Zariski sheaf property of the
plus construction, `PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq` (`PicEtAffZariskiSep.lean:137`) — nothing is glued,
so the gluing half (`PicEtAffZariskiGlue.lean`) is not used.

## What this is and is not — READ THIS BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING BELOW

It is a reduction of the *test algebra*, not of the geometry, and it does **not** prove the ring
case.  Two things are load-bearing and were wrong in an earlier version of this header; both were
found by a fresh-context audit (`I-1657`, `I-1660`) and independently reproduced here.

**1. AT A FIXED `A` the reduction is real: the ring case at `A` follows from the ring case at the
members of any finite covering family of localizations of `A`, and there is no route back.**  That
is what `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away` and `rigidity_of_away` say, and it is the usable content
of the file.

**2. UNDER THE OUTER `∀ A` IT IS NOT A WEAKENING AT ALL.**  The two `JacobianData` producers at
the bottom quantify their pointwise hypothesis over *every* test algebra — and
`Localization.Away f` **is** a test algebra, so the outer `∀ A` already covers it.  The converse
is one line with the trivial witness `f = 1`: `Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem` says `1 ∉ p`, and the
hypothesis at `Localization.Away 1` is an instance of the global statement.  So

> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton`'s hypothesis is **logically equivalent** to
> `jacobianData_of_affine_subsingleton`'s (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:296`), and
> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity`'s to `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`'s
> (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).

Those two producers are therefore **restatements, not repricings**.  They are kept because the
pointwise *shape* is what a local computation delivers, but a lane must not read them as having
reduced the obligation.  The general lesson, which cost this session a false claim: before
pricing a localisation-or-pointwise reduction as progress, try the converse with the trivial
witness — if it closes, the reduction only helps at a **fixed** base object, and the consumer's
quantifier decides whether that is any help.

**3. The interface is NOT a local-ring interface**, contrary to what this header first said.  The
hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, and `IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold
(verified: instance synthesis fails; a basic open of `Spec A` is not a point).  A lane with a
genuinely local computation holds `Localization.AtPrime p`, and **nothing here bridges `AtPrime`
to `Away`** — that bridge is spreading-out, it is unbuilt, and it is the real remaining work on
this side.

Seminormality is the other half of the story and it does not go away: see the measurement at the
end of this docstring.

## The degenerate test ring: the site is not a counterexample, and that is ALL it is

`hrigAff`'s antecedent is **vacuous** at a subsingleton `A` (there is no `k`-algebra map from
the zero ring to a field), so the hypothesis demands `q = 1` for free there.  That made the
subsingleton ring the cheapest potential *refutation* site for the affine spelling, and it was
recorded as genuinely unchecked (inbox `I-1655`, author addendum).  It is now checked:
`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` proves the plus construction **is** trivial there,

10	/-!
11	# `pic⁰` VANISHES AT EVERY FIELD TEST, AT GENUS `0`
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T` binder of the degree-zero Picard
14	vanishing is *equivalent* to the same statement at affine tests `overSpec k A`.  This file
15	discharges every **field** instance of that: at `genus C = 0`,
16	
17	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K))` for every field extension `K/k`.
18	
19	`hvan` is the hypothesis that `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` turns into a
20	`JacobianData` and that `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff`
21	shows *is* the seam's coverage antecedent at parameter `0`.  It therefore now has all of its
22	field instances closed on a genus-`0` curve, and only its **ring** instances open.
23	
24	**A COUNT CORRECTED.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called `hvan` "the hypothesis with
25	93 consumers and no producer".  That figure is from the task brief and is about
26	`JacobianData.rep`, a *different* object; restating it here made it look like a measurement of
27	`hvan`.  Measured at HEAD: the `hvan`-shaped binder occurs in **3** files, `pic0Subgroup` is
28	mentioned in 50, and `RepresentableBy` occurs 392 times.  What matters about `hvan` is not a
29	count but that both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through it and neither had an
30	instance; do not quote a number from this header — run the grep.
31	
32	## The two steps, and what each costs
33	
34	**Step 1, through the plus construction** (`eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero`).  A plus
35	class of `PicEtAff C K` is `mk E x` for some étale cover `E` of `K`; its degree is by
36	definition read on a finite separable *field* refinement of `E`
37	(`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), and `Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero` kills the transported class there.
38	Transport back is free: `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` says the plus class does not change along a
39	refinement, and `PicEtAff.mk_one` closes it.
40	
41	Note what is *not* needed: **no surjectivity of the plus unit**.  The landed
42	`PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` (`EffectivityClose.lean:141`) requires a curve section
43	over the test field, which this project constructs nowhere; the argument here never asks
44	whether the class comes from `relPic C (overSpec k K)` itself, only what happens on its own
45	cover carrier.  So the field case needs no rational point.
46	
47	**Step 2, off the degree condition** (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`).
48	Membership in `pic0Subgroup` quantifies over *all* field points of the test; at an affine test
49	over a field, the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` is one of them, and `degAt` at the identity is
50	`degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So a single instantiation of the membership binder
51	supplies the hypothesis of step 1 — the other field points are not consulted.
52	
53	## What remains, stated exactly
54	
55	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
56	
57	for `A` **not** a field.  That is fibrewise-degree-zero implies globally trivial over a base
58	ring, i.e. cohomology and base change; nothing in this tree proves it, and it is the whole
59	remaining distance from here to a `JacobianData` at a genus-`0` curve via
60	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton`.
61	
62	Two things this does **not** do, to forestall the obvious misreadings:
63	
64	* it does not compute `Pic(ℙ¹)` or any Picard group — degree-zero classes are killed without
65	  identifying the group they sit in;
66	* it says nothing at positive genus, and exhibits no positive-genus curve.
67	
68	## Main declarations
69	
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` — a plus class of degree `0` over
71	  a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.  Needs no curve section.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero` — **the field-test
73	  vanishing**.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field` — **non-vacuity at a real
75	  curve**: the same at `P1.asOver k` with *no hypothesis at all*, since
76	  `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field.
77	
78	Both are stated with **three** curve binders: `GeometricallyReduced` is unused in each
79	(measured — the linter reports it), even though the surrounding `picEt` descent material
80	carries four.
81	-/

84	
85	universe u
86	
87	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
88	
89	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
92	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
93	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
94	
95	-- Carries the base-change instance stack of the field layer through the plus quotient's
96	-- cover-refinement calculus; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap precedent.
97	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
98	/-- **A plus class of degree zero over a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.**
99	
100	`degAff` is *defined* by reading the relative degree on a finite separable field refinement of
101	the class's own cover (`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), which is exactly where the field layer
102	`relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` applies.  Transport back to the original
103	cover is free — `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` — so no comparison between covers is needed.
104	
105	**No curve section over `K` is required**, and hence no rational point: the landed plus-unit
106	surjectivity `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` is not used, because the argument works on
107	the representative's own cover carrier rather than asking the class to come from `relPic`. -/
108	theorem eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
109	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
110	    (q : PicEtAff C K) (hq : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K q = 0) : q = 1 := by
111	  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with
112	  | mk E x =>
113	    obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
114	    letI := hLf; letI := hLa; letI := hLfin; letI := hLsep
115	    letI : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
116	    haveI : IsScalarTower k K L := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
117	    -- the degree is the relative degree of the transported representative over `L`
118	    have hdeg : relPicDeg (C := C) L (relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
119	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) = 0 := by
120	      rw [← PicEtAff.degAff_mk (C := C) (K := K) E x L j]
121	      exact hq
122	    have htriv : relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
123	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = 1 :=
124	      relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C L hg _ hdeg
125	    -- transport to the field cover does not change the plus class
126	    have hstep : PicEtAff.mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L)
127	        (descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j) x)
128	        = PicEtAff.mk C E x := PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C _ x
129	    rw [← hstep]
130	    convert PicEtAff.mk_one C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L) using 2
131	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
132	    rw [descentMap_coe]
133	    have hcomp :
134	        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j).restrictScalars k
135	          = ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
136	            (j.restrictScalars k) := rfl
137	    rw [hcomp, relPicAlgMap_comp, htriv, map_one]
138	    rfl
139	
140	-- Same instance stack, plus the affine comparison.
141	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
142	/-- **THE FIELD-TEST VANISHING**: at `genus C = 0`, the degree-zero Picard group of the curve
143	vanishes at every affine test over a *field*.
144	
145	Only **one** field point of the test is consulted — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)`, at which
146	`degAt` is `degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So the `∀ K, ∀ t` binder of
147	`pic0Subgroup`'s membership is used at a single instantiation, and the remaining field points
148	carry no weight in this direction. -/
149	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero
150	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0) :
151	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) := by
152	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
153	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C K).injective ?_
154	  have hs : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) = 0 := by
155	    have h := s.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
156	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
157	  have ht : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) = 0 := by
158	    have h := t.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
159	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
160	  have h1 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) hs
161	  have h2 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) ht
162	  exact h1.trans h2.symm
163	
164	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statement fires at a curve, unconditionally -/
165	
166	/-- **The field-test vanishing at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
167	
168	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the three curve binders over an arbitrary field and
169	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`, so the theorem above applies with
170	nothing left to discharge.  Recorded because a conditional statement whose antecedent has no
171	witness is worth exactly nothing, and this one has one. -/
172	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field
173	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
174	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K)) :=
175	  subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) K
176	    (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k)
177	
178	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicAlgebra
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.EtaleCover
8	
9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/
43	
44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory
49	
50	open scoped TensorProduct
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
55	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
56	
57	noncomputable section

59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end
181	
182	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
13	test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
14	relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
15	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
16	the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
17	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
18	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
19	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
20	algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
21	which is the point of the vehicle.
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
24	  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
25	  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
27	  of test algebras.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
29	  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
30	  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
31	  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).
32	
33	Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
34	gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
35	the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
36	-/

42	open CategoryTheory

44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

46	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
47	
48	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/
53	
54	namespace PicEtAff
55	
56	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
57	
58	/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
59	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
60	  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
61	  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
62	  left_inv x := by
63	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
64	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
65	    exact mapAlg_id C x
66	  right_inv x := by
67	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
68	      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
69	    exact mapAlg_id C x
70	  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y
71	
72	@[simp]
73	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
74	    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
75	  rfl
76	
77	@[simp]
78	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
79	    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
80	  rfl
81	
82	end PicEtAff

84	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
85	
86	variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
87	
88	/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
89	the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
90	restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
91	def picEtSubgroup :
92	    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
93	  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
94	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
95	  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
96	  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
97	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
98	  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]
99	
100	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
101	level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
102	`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
103	tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
104	canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
105	def picEt : Type u :=
106	  picEtSubgroup C T
107	
108	noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
109	  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))
110	
111	namespace picEt
112	
113	variable {C T}
114	
115	/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
116	lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
117	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
118	  s.2 U V h
119	
120	@[ext]
121	lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
122	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
123	
124	variable (C T) in
125	/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
126	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
127	  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
128	    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype
129	
130	@[simp]
131	lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
132	  rfl
133	
134	@[simp]
135	lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
136	    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
141	  rfl
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=
145	  rfl
146	
147	end picEt

149	/-! ## The affine comparison -/
150	
151	section Affine
152	
153	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
154	
155	/-- The top affine open of an affine test object. -/
156	def overSpecTopAffine : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens :=
157	  ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A⟩
158	
159	/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
160	`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
161	comparison. -/
162	def picEtToAff : picEt C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A :=
163	  (PicEtAff.congr C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A)).toMonoidHom.comp
164	    (picEt.eval C (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
165	
166	lemma picEtToAff_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
167	    picEtToAff C A s
168	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
169	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	/-- The section of `picEt` over an affine test determined by a plus class of the test
173	algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse direction of the affine
174	comparison. -/
175	def picEtOfAff : PicEtAff C A →* picEt C (overSpec k A) where
176	  toFun x :=
177	    ⟨fun U => PicEtAff.mapAlg C
178	      ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
179	        (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x,
180	      fun U V h => by rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, ← AlgHom.comp_assoc,
181	        Over.resAlgHom_comp]⟩
182	  map_one' := picEt.ext fun U => map_one (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _)
183	  map_mul' x y := picEt.ext fun U => map_mul (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _) x y
184	
185	lemma picEtOfAff_val (x : PicEtAff C A) (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
186	    (picEtOfAff C A x).1 U
187	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
188	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
189	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
190	  rfl
191	
192	private lemma picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff :
193	    (picEtOfAff C A).comp (picEtToAff C A) = MonoidHom.id (picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
194	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun s => picEt.ext fun U => ?_
195	  calc ((picEtOfAff C A) (picEtToAff C A s)).1 U
196	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
197	          (((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
198	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom).comp
199	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)
200	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
201	        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
202	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top)
203	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
204	        rw [AlgHom.comp_assoc,
205	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom.comp
206	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
207	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from
208	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm_apply_apply a,
209	          AlgHom.comp_id]
210	    _ = s.1 U := s.compat U (overSpecTopAffine A) le_top
211	
212	private lemma picEtToAff_comp_picEtOfAff :
213	    (picEtToAff C A).comp (picEtOfAff C A) = MonoidHom.id (PicEtAff C A) := by
214	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x => ?_
215	  calc (picEtToAff C A) (picEtOfAff C A x)
216	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
217	          ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
218	            ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
219	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom)) x :=
220	        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
221	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (AlgHom.id k A) x := by
222	        rw [show Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) (le_top :
223	              (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens) ≤ (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens))
224	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from Over.resAlgHom_rfl _ le_top,
225	          AlgHom.id_comp,
226	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
227	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom
228	            = AlgHom.id k A from
229	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).apply_symm_apply a]
230	    _ = x := PicEtAff.mapAlg_id C x
231	
232	/-- **The affine comparison isomorphism**: on an affine test `overSpec k A`, the
233	affine-opens limit `picEt` collapses by evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the
234	affine-opens poset to the one-step plus `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra. -/
235	def picEtAffineEquiv : picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A :=
236	  MonoidHom.toMulEquiv (picEtToAff C A) (picEtOfAff C A)
237	    (picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff C A) (picEtToAff_comp_picEtOfAff C A)
238	
239	@[simp]
240	lemma picEtAffineEquiv_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
241	    picEtAffineEquiv C A s
242	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
243	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
244	  rfl
245	
246	@[simp]
247	lemma picEtAffineEquiv_symm_apply_val (x : PicEtAff C A)
248	    (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
249	    ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm x).1 U
250	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
251	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
252	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
253	  rfl
254	
255	end Affine

257	end
