136	/-- Every étale cover of a subsingleton ring has subsingleton carrier: the carrier's spectrum
137	maps **onto** `Spec A`, which is empty, so the carrier's spectrum is empty too. -/
138	theorem Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Subsingleton A]
139	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) : Subsingleton E.Carrier := by
140	  haveI : IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A) :=
141	    PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mpr ‹_›
142	  haveI : IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum E.Carrier) :=
143	    ⟨fun p => isEmptyElim (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A E.Carrier) p)⟩
144	  exact PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mp ‹_›
145	
146	/-- **The relative Picard group is trivial over a subsingleton test ring.**
147	
148	`Spec A` is empty, so the product `C ⊗ overSpec k A` is empty (project along `snd`), so its
149	Čech Picard group is trivial by the landed `Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`; the
150	quotient by `picFromBase` inherits it.
151	
152	Uses none of the curve's geometry — this is a statement about the vehicle. -/
153	theorem subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
154	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k A)) := by
155	  haveI : IsEmpty ↥((overSpec k A).left) := by
156	    change IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A)
157	    exact PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mpr ‹_›
158	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left) :=
159	    ⟨fun x _ => isEmptyElim ((snd C (overSpec k A)).left.base x)⟩
160	  haveI := Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left)
161	  exact ⟨fun x y => by
162	    induction x using relPic.ind with | mk L =>
163	    induction y using relPic.ind with | mk M =>
164	    exact congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k A)) (Subsingleton.elim L M)⟩
165	
166	/-- The `A`-algebra map into a subsingleton `A`-algebra: everything goes to `0`.  Needed
167	because two plus-class representatives over a subsingleton base live on *different* covers,
168	and `mk_eq_mk_iff` wants a common refinement. -/
169	def toSubsingletonAlgHom (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (R S : Type u)
170	    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra A R] [Algebra A S] [Subsingleton S] :
171	    R →ₐ[A] S where
172	  toFun _ := 0
173	  map_one' := Subsingleton.elim _ _
174	  map_mul' _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
175	  map_zero' := Subsingleton.elim _ _
176	  map_add' _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
177	  commutes' _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
178	
179	/-- **THE PLUS CONSTRUCTION IS TRIVIAL OVER A SUBSINGLETON TEST RING**, unconditionally.
180	
181	This is a **non-counterexample only** (audit `I-1655`/`I-1676`): the subsingleton ring is the
182	site at which `hrigAff`'s antecedent is vacuous, and therefore its cheapest potential
183	refutation site.  The conclusion holds there anyway, so the affine spelling is **not refuted**
184	at that site — but this does NOT settle `hrigAff`'s inhabitability, which remains open on
185	nonempty spectra (see the module header).  It rules out one degenerate refutation, nothing
186	more.
187	
188	No genus hypothesis, no curve input beyond the standing section variable. -/
189	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
190	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
191	  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
192	  induction x using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E ξ =>
193	  induction y using PicEtAff.ind with | _ F ζ =>
194	  haveI : Subsingleton E.Carrier := Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier E
195	  haveI : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
196	    subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton C E.Carrier
197	  refine (PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr
198	    ⟨E, AlgHom.id A _, toSubsingletonAlgHom A F.Carrier E.Carrier, ?_⟩
199	  exact Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
200	
201	/-- The `pic⁰` form at a subsingleton test ring: a subgroup of a subsingleton group. -/
202	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_subsingleton
203	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
204	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Subsingleton A] :
205	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
206	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
207	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton C (A := A)
208	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
209	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
210	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩

218	variable (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)]
219	  [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower k A (S i)]

223	member of a finite covering family of localizations of `A`, it is trivial at `A`.
224	
225	One application of the landed separation half `PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq`: two classes over `A`
226	have equal restrictions because the target is a subsingleton. -/
227	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
228	    (hloc : ∀ i, Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (S i))) :
229	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=

232	/-- **THE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at every member of a finite
233	covering family of localizations of `A` gives it at `A`.
234	
235	Note which way the field points travel, because it is what makes this cheap: a field point of a
236	localization `S i` restricts to a field point of `A` by composing with `A → S i`, so the
237	antecedent **at `A`** supplies the antecedent at each `S i` — no lifting of field points along
238	the localization is required, and no compatibility between the members is used.  The classes
239	then agree with `1` after each localization, and separation finishes. -/
240	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
241	    (hloc : ∀ i, ∀ q : PicEtAff C (S i),
242	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : S i →ₐ[k] K),
243	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
244	    (q : PicEtAff C A)
245	    (hq : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
246	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
247	    q = 1 := by
248	  refine PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq C g S hg (x := q) (y := 1) fun i => ?_
249	  rw [map_one]
250	  refine hloc i _ fun K _ _ φ => ?_
251	  rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp]
252	  exact hq K (φ.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A (S i)))

254	/-- **The reduction on the `pic⁰` carrier the producers consume**: `Subsingleton
255	(pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` from triviality of the plus construction at each member of a
256	finite covering family.
257	
258	Transported through the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv`, then restricted to the subgroup.
259	Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton`
260	(`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`) takes exactly this carrier. -/
261	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_away
262	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
263	    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
264	    (hloc : ∀ i, Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (S i))) :
265	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
266	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
267	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C g S hg hloc
268	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
269	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
270	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩

273	
274	/-! ## The pointwise form: a hypothesis at each prime, no cover supplied
275	
276	The reductions above take the covering family as an argument, which is the wrong interface for
277	a consumer: a lane computing `Pic` locally knows something *at each prime*, not a finite cover.
278	This section removes the cover from the statement.  Two elementary steps do it, and both are
279	about `Spec` rather than about the curve:
280	
281	* if a set of elements meets the complement of every prime, it generates the unit ideal
282	  (otherwise it sits inside a maximal ideal);
283	* the unit ideal is spanned by a **finite** subset (`Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`), which is
284	  the compactness of `Spec A` in the form the sheaf property wants.
285	
286	The localizations are then the canonical `Localization.Away f`, so no family of test algebras
287	has to be threaded through the statement either. -/
288	
289	section Pointwise
290	
291	/-- An indexed family of ring elements whose basic opens cover `Spec A` generates the unit ideal.
292	
293	**This is mathlib's `PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff` in another spelling**, and it is
294	written through it rather than re-proved — the audit finding `I-1659`.  An earlier version proved
295	it directly (a set in no prime is in no maximal ideal) because plain `exact?` fails on this goal;
296	`exact?` failing is not absence, and the mathlib lemma is stated as an `iSup` of basic opens over
297	an *indexed family*, which is exactly the shape the use site below has.
298	
299	Kept as a named lemma only because the `Set.range`/`iSup` translation is two tactic lines that
300	would otherwise be inlined twice. -/
301	theorem span_eq_top_of_forall_prime {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*} (f : ι → A)
302	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ i, f i ∉ p.asIdeal) :
303	    Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by
304	  rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff]
305	  ext p
306	  simpa using h p
307	
308	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
309	
310	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION**: if every prime of `A` has *some* basic open neighbourhood on
311	which the plus construction is trivial, it is trivial at `A`.
312	
313	No covering family in the statement: the witnesses are chosen at the primes, shown to span,
314	cut down to a finite subfamily by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, and fed to
315	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away`.  The hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, a BASIC OPEN and
316	NOT a local ring (`IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold); a lane holding a genuinely
317	local computation has `Localization.AtPrime p`, and the `AtPrime`-to-`Away` bridge is spreading
318	out and is unbuilt.  So this is the interface for a computation over basic opens, which is a
319	weaker thing than the header of this file originally claimed. -/
320	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime
321	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
322	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
323	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
324	  classical
325	  choose f hf hsub using h
326	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
327	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
328	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
329	  refine PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
330	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_
331	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
332	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
333	  · intro i
334	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2
335	    exact hp ▸ hsub p
336	
337	/-- The pointwise reduction on the `pic⁰` carrier the producers consume. -/
338	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime
339	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
340	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
341	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
342	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
343	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
344	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime C h
345	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
346	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
347	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
348	
349	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at a basic open around
350	each prime gives it at `A`.
351	
352	Same three steps as `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (choose, span, cut to finite), fed
353	to `PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away`.  Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
354	consumes the rigidity clause and not a `Subsingleton`, and because the rigidity form is the one
355	that carries no degree apparatus. -/
356	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime
357	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
358	      ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
359	        (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
360	          PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
361	    (q : PicEtAff C A)
362	    (hq : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
363	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
364	    q = 1 := by
365	  classical
366	  choose f hf hrig using h
367	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
368	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
369	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
370	  refine PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
371	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_ q hq
372	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
373	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
374	  · intro i
375	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2
376	    exact hp ▸ hrig p
377	
378	end Pointwise
379	
380	/-! ## The composition to the goal object
381	
382	The reductions above are worth nothing if they do not reach `JacobianData`.  These two
383	declarations are that check, and they are what makes this file usable by the representability
384	headline rather than local to its own row: the *pointwise-local* hypothesis, quantified over
385	every test algebra, produces the datum through the landed producers with no atlas, no chart
386	certificate, no coverage clause, no divisor representability and no rational point.
387	
388	Both carry the genus-`0` hypothesis of the producer they compose with, and neither adds anything
389	else. -/
390	
391	section Datum
392	
393	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
394	
395	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local vanishing.**
396	
397	`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime` at every test algebra, fed to
398	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`).  The
399	hypothesis mentions no test object, no open and no morphism of schemes: only `k`-algebras, their
400	primes, and the plus construction at the canonical localizations. -/
401	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton
402	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
403	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
404	        Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
405	    JacobianData C :=
406	  jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton C fun A _ _ =>
407	    subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime C (h A)
408	
409	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local rigidity**, at genus `0`.
410	
411	The rigidity analogue, through `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
412	(`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).  This is the shortest statement of the whole vanishing
413	route's remaining debt IN SHAPE, though — per point 2 of the module docstring — not in
414	strength: this hypothesis is logically equivalent to `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`'s own. -/
415	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0)
416	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
417	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
418	        ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
419	          (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
420	            PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1) :
421	    JacobianData C :=
422	  jacobianData_of_rigidityAff C hg fun A _ _ => PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime C (h A)
423	
424	/-! ### The equivalence, proved rather than asserted
425	
426	Point 2 of the module docstring says the two producers above are restatements.  A docstring
427	saying so is a claim nobody checks, so here it is as a theorem: the converse direction, with the
428	trivial witness `f = 1`.  Together with `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (which is the
429	forward direction) the two hypotheses are interderivable, and the same argument works verbatim for
430	the rigidity spelling.
431	
432	This is the check that should be run on *any* localisation-or-pointwise reduction before it is
433	priced as progress. -/
434	
435	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
436	/-- **The converse, with the trivial witness**: the global hypothesis implies the pointwise-local
437	one, because `Localization.Away 1` is itself a test algebra and `1` lies outside every prime.
438	
439	So under the outer `∀ A` the pointwise form is *not* weaker — the content of the audit finding
440	`I-1660`, kept in the file so the equivalence cannot be lost again. -/
441	theorem forall_prime_subsingleton_of_forall
442	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A))
443	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
444	    ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f)) :=
445	  ⟨1, fun hc => p.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ hc isUnit_one),
446	    h (Localization.Away (1 : A))⟩
447	
448	end Datum
449	
450	end
451	
452	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TwoChartRepresentable
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TwoChartHonest
8	
9	/-!
10	# A CHART-TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS IS TRIVIAL WHEN THE OVERLAP UNITS ARE ALL COBOUNDARIES
11	
12	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of
13	the two-chart comparison
14	
15	```
16	Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  ↪  X.CechPic
17	```
18	
19	— surjectivity onto the chart-trivial classes (`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial`,
20	`Tangent/TwoChartRepresentable.lean:301`) and the exact kernel
21	(`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`, `Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean:321`).  Composing them
22	gives a **criterion** nobody had stated: if every overlap unit is a coboundary, then every class
23	trivial on both charts is trivial.
24	
25	That composite is what a computation of `Pic` on a two-chart cover actually wants to consume: it
26	turns a statement about the *unit groups of three rings* — pure commutative algebra, no
27	cohomology — into triviality of a Picard class.  Both inputs are general in the scheme, so this
28	is too: no affineness, no curve, no dual numbers, no field.
29	
30	## Why it is here rather than in `Tangent/`
31	
32	The two inputs were built for the Wave-5 `ε`-kernel computation and live there.  This file is
33	about the *Picard group of a two-chart scheme* rather than about tangent spaces, and its intended
34	consumer is the ring-case obligation of the representability route
35	(`Picard/Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean`), where the relevant `X` is a relative curve over a test ring
36	and the three rings are the two chart algebras and their overlap.
37	
38	## The one hypothesis that is not about units
39	
40	`hsel`, surjectivity of the selector, is what makes the two-chart cover *honest* (both charts are
41	actually used).  It is not an extra obligation:
42	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine`
43	(`Tangent/TwoChartHonest.lean:108`) derives it from `¬ IsAffine X` alone, and a proper
44	positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not affine.  Stated with `hsel` explicit because this
45	file is general in `X` and the non-affineness is the consumer's to supply.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48	
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the
50	  criterion.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the same as a
52	  statement about the subgroup of chart-trivial classes, for a consumer holding two classes
53	  rather than one.
54	-/
55	
56	set_option autoImplicit false
57	
58	universe u
59	
60	open CategoryTheory
61	
62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	namespace Scheme
65	
66	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : Bool → X.Opens}
67	
68	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the overlap units of a two-chart cover: the units of
69	`Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` that are products of restrictions of chart units.  Abbreviation for the
70	`TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two restriction maps, so that the statements below read. -/
71	noncomputable abbrev twoChartCoboundaryUnits (V : Bool → X.Opens) :
72	    Subgroup Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ :=
73	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
74	    (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
75	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
76	
77	/-- **THE CRITERION**: on a two-chart cover whose overlap units are *all* coboundaries, a Picard
78	class trivial on both charts is trivial.
79	
80	Composite of the two landed halves of the two-chart comparison: surjectivity presents the class
81	as `twoChartClassHom` of an overlap unit, and the kernel description kills it because that unit
82	is a coboundary by hypothesis.
83	
84	Completely general in `X`: no affineness, no curve, no field, no dual numbers.  The content is
85	that `hcob` is a statement about the unit groups of three rings — so a consumer computes
86	`Pic` on a two-chart cover by computing units, with no cohomology in sight. -/
87	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary
88	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
89	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
90	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1) :
91	    L = 1 := by
92	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial sel hmem L hL
93	  rw [← hu]
94	  exact (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr (hcob u)
95	
96	/-- The criterion for a consumer holding two classes: chart-trivial classes form a subsingleton.
97	
98	Note this is *not* `Subsingleton X.CechPic` — the chart-triviality hypothesis is on the classes,
99	not on the scheme, and a class nontrivial on a chart is untouched. -/
100	theorem subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary
101	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
102	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
103	    {L M : X.CechPic}
104	    (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
105	    (hM : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι M = 1) :
106	    L = M := by
107	  rw [cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary sel hmem hsel hcob L hL,
108	    cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary sel hmem hsel hcob M hM]
109	
110	/-- The criterion with `hsel` discharged from non-affineness, which is how a curve consumer meets
111	it: a proper positive-dimensional scheme over a field is not affine, and
112	`surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine` turns that single fact into the selector surjectivity.
113	
114	Takes the cover as an `AffineTwoCover` because that is the carrier the discharge lemma is stated
115	against. -/
116	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary_of_not_isAffine
117	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : Y.AffineTwoCover) (hY : ¬ IsAffine Y)
118	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(Y, D.boolFamily false ⊓ D.boolFamily true)ˣ,
119	      u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits D.boolFamily)
120	    (L : Y.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (D.boolFamily s).ι L = 1) :
121	    L = 1 :=
122	  cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary D.selector D.selector_mem
123	    (D.surjective_selector_of_not_isAffine hY) hcob L hL
124	
125	/-! ## The form with a payable hypothesis
126	
127	The universal hypothesis `hcob` above is **false** at the case the representability route cares
128	about: for `ℙ¹` over a domain, `t` is an overlap unit and is not a coboundary
129	(`not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`, `Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`) — which is just
130	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`.  So a consumer given only the criterion above would set out to prove something
131	untrue.
132	
133	The repair is to constrain only the units that *present the class in question*, which is what
134	surjectivity hands over anyway.  Two things are worth saying about it explicitly, because the
135	obvious repair is a trap:
136	
137	* the `↔` version — "`L = 1` iff some presenting unit is a coboundary" — is **vacuous**: its
138	  forward direction takes the presenting unit to be `1`, and the chart-triviality hypothesis is
139	  never consulted (measured: the unused-variable linter flags it).  So the useful form is the
140	  implication with a `∀` over presenting units, below, where both hypotheses are consumed;
141	* that form is *strictly weaker* than `hcob`, and demonstrably so: `hcob` implies it by ignoring
142	  the presentation equation (`forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary`). -/
143	
144	/-- **THE CRITERION WITH A PAYABLE HYPOTHESIS**: a chart-trivial class is trivial as soon as
145	*every unit presenting it* is a coboundary.
146	
147	Both hypotheses are consumed — `hL` produces the presenting unit through surjectivity, and
148	`hpres` is applied to exactly that unit.  Unlike the universal form this is not refuted by
149	`ℙ¹`: there the presenting units of a *degree-zero* class are the exponent-zero Laurent units,
150	which are precisely the coboundaries (`mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff`). -/
151	theorem cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary
152	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
153	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : ∀ s : Bool, Scheme.CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1)
154	    (hpres : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
155	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V) :
156	    L = 1 := by
157	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial sel hmem L hL
158	  rw [← hu]
159	  exact (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr (hpres u hu)
160	
161	/-- The universal hypothesis implies the presenting-unit one, by ignoring the presentation
162	equation.  Recorded so that "strictly weaker" is a proved relation rather than a reading of the
163	two statements — the weakening is what makes the hypothesis payable at `ℙ¹`. -/
164	theorem forall_presenting_of_forall_coboundary
165	    (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x))
166	    (hcob : ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ, u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V)
167	    (L : X.CechPic) :
168	    ∀ u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ,
169	      twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = L → u ∈ twoChartCoboundaryUnits V :=
170	  fun u _ => hcob u
171	
172	end Scheme
173	
174	end AlgebraicGeometry
